A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CSIvA study and contain readable main text, 16 figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–E, including proofs. The formatting and pagination differences do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original CSIvA experiments on synthetic causal models and Tübingen, Sachs, AutoMPG, and Sprinkler datasets in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains the original synthetic and real-data evaluations in Section 4 and Appendix D, with revised results in Figure 1a.

M1.justification: CSIvA’s embeddings, alternating attention, encoder–decoder architecture, autoregressive graph prediction, and maximum-likelihood objective remain unchanged. The mixed-SCM training procedures are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same bivariate SCM classes, noise distributions, neural-network and Gaussian-process mechanisms, independent-pair scenarios, and four named real-data collections. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains DirectLiNGAM and NoGAM; Appendix D retains DirectLiNGAM, CAM, NoGAM, and GraNDAG. AdaScore and LNMIX are newly discussed in Section 4.5 but are not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1, Table 1, and Appendix D retain the dataset sizes, preprocessing, SHD metric, model configuration, optimization settings, and training-budget comparisons. The clarified description of sampling individual SCM instances does not establish a changed generation procedure.

E4.justification: The mechanism/noise-shift tests, identifiability examples, training-size analyses, independent-graph experiments, larger mixed-training budgets, and Gaussian-process checks are retained. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three training runs with different initializations and training samples, evaluation on 1,500 test datasets, and 95% confidence intervals. Figure 1a’s changed error-bar values do not change the reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 1a increases CSIvA’s reported SHD on linear-Beta data from zero to approximately 0.15 and on linear-Gumbel data from near zero to approximately 0.17, with corresponding error-bar changes. DirectLiNGAM remains near zero, and the other results are retained. The stated settings match, but these revisions are unexplained.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds the cited identifiability result for linear Gaussian models with equal noise variances. The mathematical definitions, counterexample, post-ANM reduction, and formal results and proofs in Appendices C and E remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract reframes mixed training as investigating when generalization improves and limits its concluding statement to amortized discovery with transformers. The first introduction contribution is explicitly described as empirical. The central identifiability and mixed-training conclusions remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 recasts Hypothesis 1 as an informal expectation about test generalization and explicitly emphasizes empirical investigation. Section 4.5 revises the classical-method applicability discussion from nonlinear mechanisms to linear and nonlinear additive-noise models, refining the mechanism/noise tradeoff.

D1.justification: v3 adds separate links to the CSIvA implementation and experiment-reproduction code in Section 4, footnote 1; v2 provides no corresponding links. Appendix B’s hyperparameters, data-generation details, and computing-resource information are retained.

R1.justification: Adds Brown et al. (2020), Peters and Bühlmann (2013), Immer et al. (2023), Xi et al. (2025), Montagna et al. (2025), and Liu et al. (2024). These extend the background and update the discussion of classical methods without substantially changing the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the abstract, hypothesis, SCM-sampling explanation, and justification for studying bivariate graphs. Affiliation and publication text also change, while section organization is retained. v3 introduces awkward duplicated references such as 'Equation equation 7'.

P2.justification: The paper is comprehensively retypeset into the TMLR layout, changing typography, text width, running headers, captions, and figure placement. The hypothesis is boxed and Figure 1 is rerendered. All figures and the table remain, but Figures 14–16 now interrupt the opening of Appendix E.

improvement.justification: The new code-access information, clearer empirical framing, and added identifiability qualification modestly improve reproducibility documentation and claim precision. These gains outweigh limited presentation regressions, including interrupted appendix text and duplicated equation references. The unexplained Figure 1a revisions do not establish improved evidential reliability.
